acceptance: A regression package whose module-local graph imports no escape hatch is derivable and can be skipped (red test first)
A package that reaches os through a module package (apicover via acsassert) stays an escape hatch
The shadow soak records would_skip > 0 for a change that touches no dependency of some regression package
fix: TDD first. Judge the escape hatches on the module's own packages only: list `-deps -test -f '{{.ImportPath}}|{{join .Imports}}'`, walk the module packages that the regression test package reaches, and mark it an escape hatch only when one of them (or the test package) imports os, os/exec or os/user directly. Keep TestResolveDeps_DropsPredicatesThatReachOutsideTheImportGraph green (apicover reaches os through acsassert, a module package). Add a real-tree test that at least one regression package is derivable. 100% coverage, zero comments, update docs/architecture/packages/internal-regressiontia.md and ADR-0082.
summary: Found while fixing the review of PR #1098 (2026-10-21). regressiontia.listCorpusDeps lists `{{join .Deps}}` (every transitive dependency) and resolveDeps marks a package as an escape hatch when any of them is os, os/exec or os/user. Each test package reaches os through the standard package testing (`go list -deps testing` includes os), so every regression package is an escape hatch, Select always puts it in Selected, and would_skip is 0 in every cycle. The regression_tia shadow soak therefore measures nothing, and its 'zero misses' condition for enforce holds by construction.
title: Regression TIA: the escape-hatch check reads transitive deps, so the selection never skips a package
